title: Sustainability & Cost Ops: Quick Battlecard for Platform Sellers
body:
Purpose:
A concise pocket battlecard for platform sellers to engage infrastructure/platform engineering buyers concerned about carbon footprint, GPU utilization efficiency, and long-term operating expense. This is intentionally short-form (1 pager + 4 quick slides) for use in calls and handoffs to solutions engineering.

Top-line value props (elevator lines):
- "Reduce tokens = reduce watts": show how prefix/KV caching + adaptive batching can cut per-request compute by 20–70% depending on workload patterns.
- "Lower $ / prediction without sacrificing quality": quantization + model variant routing maintains accuracy while trimming unit cost.
- "Operational controls for green SLOs": routing policies and autoscale caps let you set energy/cost budgets per route.

Buyer personas and pain signals to listen for:
- Platform/Inference Lead: worried about monthly GPU spend and internal chargeback noise. Signal: "we're over-allocated on tails" or "costs spike unpredictably".
- Security/Compliance Platform PM: wants compute locality and policy on on-prem vs cloud for regulated data. Signal: asks about private deployment energy auditing.
- Sustainability/ESG Program Manager: looks for carbon reporting and vendor-level sustainability claims. Signal: asks for meterable emission reductions or supplier data.

Key metrics to have ready on call (ask for or present):
- Baseline tokens/day and 95/99th latency targets
- Current GPU fleet utilization and tail percentiles
- Average request sequence length and prefix reuse rate
- Current monthly inference spend (cloud + infra)

Win themes and positioning (short hooks):
- Predictable economics: reserved pools + autoscale ceilings reduce billing surprises.
- Measurable improvement: typical pilots show 25–40% unit-cost reduction via batching/caching + variant routing.
- Compliance-friendly deployment: private/VPC installs and KMS/HSM integrations enable secure on-prem audits for energy use.

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "We can’t reduce latency by batching": "We use continuous batching with latency SLOs and can set end-to-end targets; for critical routes we recommend adaptive small-batch mode or model variants optimized for low-latency."
- "Quantization will hurt model outputs": "We do A/B evals and quality regressions are tracked in Redwood Optimize; we can run a shadow test on your prompt set and present token-level quality deltas."
- "ESG claims are marketing": "We provide measurable before/after metrics tied to concrete changes (kv cache hit rates, tokens avoided, GPU-hours saved) and can integrate with your carbon accounting system via simple export hooks."

Quick pilot blueprint (4–6 week):
1) Discovery (week 0–1): collect token profiles, current infra costs, critical routes, and SLOs.
2) Small pilot (week 1–3): enable prefix/KV caching + adaptive batching on a non-critical route (5–10% of traffic), baseline A/B logging.
3) Measure (week 3–4): present unit-cost, latency distribution, cache hit rate, and simulated carbon-hours saved.
4) Scale & rollout (week 4–6): extend to more routes, introduce model variant routing and reserved capacity if warranted.

Pricing & commercial levers to mention:
- Host: show incremental savings on per-token price when applying Redwood Optimize recommendations; emphasize that lower per-token cost is achieved without changing price list (it's operational).
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with caps can be used as a budgeting instrument to stabilize monthly spend.
- Private: license + support model; highlight that customers often offset license cost with lower on-prem GPU hours.

Data & audit artifacts we can provide in pilot:
- Token-by-token cost breakdown and saved tokens CSV
- Cache hit-rate dashboard exports and KV reuse traces
- GPU-hours consumed pre/post pilot and conversion to CO2e using customer's region factor
- Regression report on prompt test-set with example diffs and human-review flags

Slide outline for the mini-deck (for SDR/AE to use in a follow-up):
- Slide 1: One-line problem + Redwood solution (customer quote style)
- Slide 2: Pilot blueprint with timelines and roles (what SE needs from buyer)
- Slide 3: Example results (sample numbers from anonymized pilot)
- Slide 4: Commercial options + next steps (PO/POC, SE intro)

Suggested call-to-action scripts (one-liners):
- Initial call close: "If you can share a week of token logs and your 95/99 latency targets, our SE team can run the first shadow pilot in 7–10 days."
- Post-demo: "We’ll set up a 30-minute kickoff with infra, SE, and your sustainability owner to align metrics — then we run a low-risk pilot for 3 weeks."

Handoff checklist for SE after seller wins interest:
- Access: S3/endpoint for token logs, list of critical routes, contact for infra + ESG owner
- Targets: target cost reduction %, latency SLOs, accepted quality delta thresholds
- Tools: assign canary route, enable KV cache, set batching profile, schedule nightly regression report

Notes to seller (internal tips):
- Use the example numbers conservatively — buyers expect real metrics. Frame claims as "typical pilot outcomes" and offer to show anonymized examples.
- If the buyer is cloud-only and cost-focused, prioritize reserved capacity + model variant routing. If on-prem or regulated, lead with private deployment and audit artifacts.
- Keep the sustainability conversation technical and measurable; avoid marketing-only language.

Appendix: sample short email to prospect (to copy/paste)
Subject: Quick pilot to reduce inference spend & surface sustainability metrics
Hi <Name>,
We run a short 3-week pilot that typically reduces inference unit-costs by ~25–40% while keeping latency and quality targets. If you can share a week of token logs and your top 3 critical routes, we’ll prototype caching and batching on a non-critical route and return a measurable before/after report. Can we set a 30-min kickoff next week?
Thanks,
Evelyn
